title: Ngaju language - Wikipedia
text: 1 month ago - Ngaju (also Ngaju Dayak or Dayak Ngaju) is an Austronesian language spoken along the Kapuas, Kahayan, Katingan, and Mentaya Rivers in Central Kalimantan, Indonesia. It is closely related to the Bakumpai language.

title: Dayak, Ngaju in Indonesia people group profile | Joshua Project
text: Ngaju Dayak families often live in villages along rivers, where homes are built on stilts to withstand flooding. Farming is a major part of life, with rice, vegetables, and fruit grown in small plots. Fishing and gathering forest products supplement their diet. Community life is close-knit, and extended families often live near one another. Celebrations include traditional music, dance, and ceremonies that mark life events such as harvest and marriage.
